method: Lightweight, not continuous 30s sampling during the sweep (not built into this session in time): a post-sweep snapshot plus one live probe with splash still resident.
ollama_gemma4_evidence: 'ollama ps' immediately after the sweep finished showed gemma4:26b-a4b-it-q4_K_M-ctx32k still resident (18GB, 100% GPU, num_ctx=65536, 10 min keep-alive remaining) — it was never evicted across arm A (sequential ollama), arm C (splash-only), or arm D (concurrent ollama), despite splash holding ~15.9GB resident throughout arm C.
concurrent_conversation_evidence: One live compliance-reading conversation turn through the deployed router, fired immediately after the sweep completed with splash still loaded and idle: HTTP 200, wall 10.68s, answered normally. Not fired DURING active sweep load (the sweep had just finished) — this is evidence the product surface recovers promptly and models coexist at rest, not proof of latency under simultaneous load.
caveat: A true concurrent-load test (a conversation turn fired WHILE arm C or D is actively generating) was not run — doing so would have meant a fourth live sweep pass, and the speed/completion findings already answer whether splash is worth adopting at this config. Recorded as an open item rather than a claim this receipt does not support.
